before: Absolute error is the distance between a forecast and its outcome. Mean absolute error averages that distance over the selected observations. It describes that evaluation set; it does not establish how a model will perform in another period.

An interval needs a separate check: how often did outcomes fall inside the stated range, and how wide was it? Wide intervals can cover many outcomes without being useful. Calibration needs enough independent observations and an explicit evaluation window.
after: Absolute error is the size of the gap between a forecast and its outcome. Mean absolute error averages those gaps across the forecasts being tested. It describes that sample, not how the model will perform in another period.

A forecast range needs a separate test. How often did it contain the outcome, and how wide was it? A wide range can contain many outcomes while telling you little. Testing whether ranges match their stated confidence level needs enough independent observations over a clearly defined period.
note: Retains error definition, sample limit, coverage versus width and calibration requirements; explains calibration rather than leaving jargon unexplained.
